body:
## Summary

Implements the issue-first, zero-credential episode-ingest pipeline agreed in #76. A scheduled collector detects newly published podcast episodes from the [Anchor RSS feed](https://anchor.fm/s/10dbf5b7c/podcast/rss) and files a templated `@sepo-agent /implement` issue (mirroring #31/#75) so the existing `agent-router` → `agent-implement` pipeline opens the website PR for review.

- **`.agent/src/episode-ingest.ts`** — pure, dependency-free logic: parse the feed, detect the lowest-numbered episode not yet under `content/episodes/epNN.md`, convert the HTML description to readable text, and derive external links with **no API keys**:
  - Apple Podcasts → iTunes Lookup API, matched on `episodeGuid`
  - Spotify → server-rendered `open.spotify.com/embed/show/...` `__NEXT_DATA__`
  - YouTube → `yt-dlp` channel listing, title-matched with a most-recent-upload fallback
- **`.agent/src/cli/episode-ingest.ts`** — fetches the sources, downloads the cover, and emits Action outputs. Every lookup degrades gracefully: a missing link is flagged in the issue rather than failing the run.
- **`.github/workflows/agent-episode-ingest.yml`** — hourly `schedule` + `workflow_dispatch`; installs `yt-dlp`, runs the collector, dedupes against existing issues by title, and files the `/implement` issue using the resolved agent token so the router picks it up.
- **`.agent/src/__tests__/episode-ingest.test.ts`** — 10 unit tests over an RSS fixture covering parsing, dedup, description conversion, and link extraction/matching.

## Verification

- `npm run build` clean; full `.agent` suite green (723 tests, including the 10 new ones).
- Live end-to-end dry run against the real feed detected episode 5 and produced links identical to those hand-filed in #75 — YouTube `Vh_j64tVGFQ`, Spotify `7GRrw4m3GDq4thvQUff4TV`, Apple `i=1000771878436` — plus a 3000×3000 cover download.
- Workflow YAML parse, `gh`-token lint, and `git diff --check` all pass.

## Notes

- No secrets are stored in the repo. The YouTube Data API key discussed in #76 remains a backup only if `yt-dlp` is ever hard-blocked from CI.
- The collector is deterministic; the episode page, guest page, cross-links, and cover commit are handled by the existing agent pipeline from the generated issue.

Closes #76

comments.body: @lolipopshock I am thinking of merging this.  Should automate our website updates on episode release in the future.  Any thoughts?

@sepo-agent /answer Would this pipeline break if we ever update an episode title?  Or what if we want to trigger an episode change like fixing a thumbnail?  I assume this wouldn't propagate that change?  This isn't a big deal, but the pipeline actually breaking is a big deal so might be something to flag if it would be brittle.

Good — your assumption is correct, and the reassuring part is that updates can't *break* the pipeline. Here's the precise behavior:

## Would a title change break it? No.

Detection keys off the **episode number**, not the title. [`findNewEpisode`](https://github.com/augmented-mind/augmented-mind.github.io/blob/pr80/.agent/src/episode-ingest.ts#L123-L128) only returns feed items whose number is **not** already present as a `content/episodes/epNN.md` file ([`getExistingEpisodeNumbers`](https://github.com/augmented-mind/augmented-mind.github.io/blob/pr80/.agent/src/episode-ingest.ts#L104-L117)). The number itself comes from the feed's `<itunes:episode>` tag, with a `#N` / "episode N" title fallback ([`parseFeedItems`](https://github.com/augmented-mind/augmented-mind.github.io/blob/pr80/.agent/src/episode-ingest.ts#L80-L101)).

So if you rename episode 5's title after `ep05.md` exists, the collector sees `5 ∈ existing`, filters it out, and does nothing. No error, no refile. The run is a clean no-op.

## Would a thumbnail fix (or any edit) propagate? No — by design.

There is **no update/sync path**. The pipeline is strictly *create-once*: it only ever acts on episode numbers that have no `epNN.md` yet. Any edit to an already-ingested episode — cover art, description, links, title — will simply not propagate to the site. Your assumption is exactly right.

This is reinforced by two independent guards, so even forcing a re-run won't double-file:
- **File existence** gates detection (above).
- **Issue-title dedup** in the workflow skips creation if a `Release Episode N` issue exists in **any** state — open *or closed* ([workflow L91-103](https://github.com/augmented-mind/augmented-mind.github.io/blob/pr80/.github/workflows/agent-episode-ingest.yml#L91-L103)).

## The one brittleness worth noting (minor)

The dedup guard matches on the **exact issue title** `Release Episode N`. The body carries a stable `guid:` marker ([L297](https://github.com/augmented-mind/augmented-mind.github.io/blob/pr80/.agent/src/episode-ingest.ts#L296-L299)), but the workflow doesn't use it for dedup — only the title. So if someone manually renames the filed issue *before* `epNN.md` lands, the next hourly run could refile a duplicate. That's a duplicate-issue annoyance, not a pipeline break, and the file-existence guard closes it permanently once the PR merges.

## Bottom line

- **Title/thumbnail edits won't break the pipeline** — worst case is a silent no-op.
- **They won't propagate either** — re-publishing an episode's metadata is out of scope here; updating live episode content stays a manual edit (or a future enhancement).

If you ever *want* update propagation, the natural extension would be a content-hash marker per episode that the collector diffs against the feed — but that's a deliberate feature, not a gap that makes the current design fragile.

## Rubrics Update

No changes were committed to [`agent/rubrics`](https://github.com/augmented-mind/augmented-mind.github.io/tree/agent/rubrics) from PR #80.

Created one draft rubric.

**Summary of changes:**

Added `rubrics/review_quality/flag-automation-brittleness.yaml` — a `draft`/`should` rubric capturing a durable preference from PR #80: when working on automation/CI pipelines, agents should proactively flag brittleness and failure modes (what breaks on upstream changes, silent no-ops, run errors), distinguishing "won't propagate" (acceptable) from "will break" (must flag).

**Rationale:**
- Sourced from XenonMolecule's explicit comment on the episode-ingest pipeline PR asking the agent to flag brittleness — a stable robustness value for the team's automation work, not a one-off. XenonMolecule is this run's requester and the merge decision-maker here.
- Marked `draft` because it rests on a single (though authoritative) comment, and both human participants show `CONTRIBUTOR` association rather than confirmed OWNER/MEMBER.

**Skipped** (not rubric-worthy): the surge preview bot comment, the `/review`/`/answer` slash commands, and the agent's own answer output — all advisory bot output or one-off routing, with no additional durable preference signal.

No prior `/rubrics/` directory or rubrics branch existed, so this is the first rubric.
